hints: Look closely at P, it has two different functional groups that can each make an ester, so focus on which group reacts with which type of compound.
Remember that concentrated sulfuric acid signals esterification, and effervescence with sodium means R must still contain an $-OH$ or $-COOH$ group to give $H_2$.
Think about what happens when P is in excess, only one molecule of Q reacts, so one group on P is used up and the other is left free to react with sodium.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups in P**

P is 3-hydroxy-3-methylbutanoic acid, $(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2COOH$. It has a tertiary alcohol $-OH$ and a carboxylic acid $-COOH$.

So P can act as an alcohol or as an acid in esterification.

**Recall what conc. sulfuric acid does**

Concentrated $H_2SO_4$ is the catalyst for esterification:
$$\text{carboxylic acid + alcohol} \rightleftharpoons \text{ester + water}$$
So Q must be a carboxylic acid or an alcohol to form an ester R.

**Use the excess and sodium clues**

P is in excess, so each molecule of Q reacts with only one molecule of P. Only one functional group of P is esterified.

Pure R gives effervescence with $Na$:
$$2ROH + 2Na \rightarrow 2RONa + H_2$$
$$2RCOOH + 2Na \rightarrow 2RCOONa + H_2$$
This proves R must still have a free $-OH$ or $-COOH$ group.

**Test each possible Q**

1 with P: $CH_3COOH$ reacts with the alcohol $-OH$ of P to give an ester, leaving the $-COOH$ of P free. R still fizzes with Na. This works.

2 with P: $CH_3CH_2OH$ reacts with the $-COOH$ of P to give an ester, leaving the tertiary alcohol $-OH$ of P free. R still fizzes with Na. This works.

3 with P: propanone is a ketone. It does not undergo esterification. No ester R is formed. This fails.

Therefore only 1 and 2 can be Q.

options.A: Incorrect. This option includes 1, 2 and 3. While 1 and 2 both form esters that retain a group reactive toward sodium, 3 is propanone, a ketone, which does not undergo esterification with P under these conditions.
options.B: Correct. 1 (ethanoic acid) esterifies the tertiary alcohol of P leaving its carboxylic acid free, and 2 (ethanol) esterifies the carboxylic acid of P leaving its alcohol free. In both cases, with P in excess, R retains an $O-H$ group and gives $H_2$ effervescence with Na.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes 2 and 3 but omits 1. Compound 2 is correct, but 3 cannot react, and 1 is wrongly left out. Ethanoic acid readily esterifies the alcohol group of P.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. Compound 1 is correct, but compound 2 is also correct and is wrongly excluded. Ethanol readily esterifies the carboxylic acid group of P.
